leads.name: Brackenridge Park numbered heritage trees (#95, #100, #101, #139, #141)
leads.species: Live Oak (Quercus virginiana/fusiformis), Pecan (Carya illinoinensis), Bald Cypress (Taxodium distichum)
leads.reason: Found via the City of San Antonio's own commissioned tree-ring dating study (Joe Buck / Cross Timbers Dendro Consulting, Jan 2023 final report, sanantonio.gov PDF), which cored five of the city's officially designated 'heritage trees' (>24in diameter) near the river wall/Japanese Tea Garden area of Brackenridge Park. NOT PROMOTED to verified this pass: ring-count dating found tree #139 (pecan) 82-92 years old, #100 (live oak) 75-81 years, #95 (live oak) 73-79 years, #141 (bald cypress) only 34-38 years old. All are heritage-SIZED but none is centuries-old; they qualify for the city's diameter-based designation but not for this project's 'genuinely old' bar. #101 (a large live oak) could not be cored (borer broke) but the surveyor's professional opinion is it is unlikely to be old either. Recorded here so a future pass does not re-chase these five specific numbered trees as ancient-tree candidates; they could still be considered on visual/historic-park grounds if a future pass wants to build a Brackenridge Park cluster, but not on age.
leads.source: City of San Antonio Parks and Recreation / Cross Timbers Dendro Consulting LLC, Jan 2023 (https://www.sanantonio.gov/Portals/0/Files/Parks/BrackenRidgeMasterPlan/Brackenridge%20Park%20Tree-Ring%20Dating%20Project.pdf)

leads.name: Burnt Oak
leads.reason: A huge live oak on the east bank of Salado Creek, roughly 50 feet tall and 22 feet round per the finding aid, standing near where Stephen F. Austin's Texian army camped in October 1835 before the siege of Bexar. About 300 yards north of the East Southcross crossing, which puts it on or by the Salado Creek Greenway. Needs: an independent source beyond the Forest Service (none found in this pass), alive confirmation, and whether the trunk is on public greenway land.

location.address: Salado Creek, about 300 yards north of East Southcross Boulevard, San Antonio

leads.name: The Taco Land Live Oak
leads.reason: 2026-10-22 write pass: held back, not shipped. Stands on a commercial lot (the former Taco Land bar, 103 W Grayson St, planned as a Velvet Taco with a patio per SA Current 2021); whether a visitor can reach it without being a customer, or whether the restaurant opened with the tree kept, is not established (hard rule 10). No statement of the tree after 2021, and the pin is the building's address point, not the trunk. Verified facts kept below; ship once a source or reader confirms it stands and can be seen from the street or an open patio.

location.address: 103 W Grayson St, San Antonio, TX 78212 (former Taco Land, now Velvet Taco site)

leads.verify_notes: FLAGGED: alive and access both thin. San Antonio Report 'Heritage Tree: The Live Oak at Taco Land' (Maeckle, 10 June 2012, updated 31 Jan 2020): 103 West Grayson Street, west bank of the river, 25 yards from the water (which the article says explains its size and health). Figures from the article's box: circumference 14 ft 4 in (437 cm), DBH 4 ft 7 in, 37 ft tall (11 m), canopy 70 ft. Age: local lore says over 500 years; City Forester Michael Nentwich doubts it and suggests 100 to 200 years (box: 'Probably 100-200 years'). Use 100 to 200, never the 500 lore as fact. Context: Taco Land, a punk and rock bar, has been closed since a 2005 robbery in which founder Ram Ayala and a doorman were killed (as stated in the article). New owners David Adelman and Ricardo Chavira hired an arborist to prune it and planned an outdoor bar removing the concrete patio and tin roof so the roots could thrive. SA Current (8 Jan 2021, updated 5 Aug 2024) says the Velvet Taco on the former site would keep 'some of the building's original murals and trademark oak tree' (implies retained, does not say so outright). Address discrepancy: 101 W Grayson (SA Current) vs 103 W Grayson (SA Report, Velvet Taco release, TDLR filing). Pin is the OSM address point for 103 W Grayson (Nominatim 29.44464,-98.48174), the building, not the trunk: approximate. No post-2021 statement of the tree seen; not a heritage-tree designation by itself (the series' title is not an official register). Two news sources, neither a register.
